What Is Specialty Powder Coating?

Specialty powder coating is a dry finishing process for unusual, one-off or custom metal parts, in which electrostatically charged powder is sprayed onto the part and heated in an oven until it cures into a hard, even layer. It suits work that does not fit a standard production run.

The finish is made from thermoset powder, which cures with heat instead of drying like liquid paint. At a cure temperature of 180 to 200 °C, the powder flows, bonds to the metal and hardens into one continuous coating without runs or drips. That makes it a dependable corrosion-resistant and chip-resistant choice for parts that face weather, handling and wear. As a form of specialty metal finishing, it is often chosen where a part is hard to replace.

Typical projects include one-off parts, test builds, custom fabrications and decorative metalwork, along with metal sculptures from artists and makers. Good one-off powder coating depends on planning each job from the bare metal up, so our specialty powder coating is planned around the part in front of us, not a standard recipe. Our wider [powder coating services](/services) cover the full range of work we do.
Our Specialty Powder Coating Process

Our specialty powder coating process has six stages: intake and inspection, cleaning and pretreatment, masking, powder application, oven curing and final inspection. Each stage is documented, so a repeat of your project matches the first piece. The same controls support our [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) work.
Step 1 – Intake and Inspection

We check each part for rust, old coatings, weld seams and damage, then confirm the finish and your timing. Unusual shapes are studied first, because hanging a part so every surface can be reached is often the hardest step on a single job.
Step 2 – Cleaning and Pretreatment

Parts are washed and chemically treated so the powder bonds to clean metal. Skipping this stage is a common reason finishes fail early. Parts that need old coatings removed first may suit our [powder coat stripping and recoating](/services/restoration-recoating) service.
Step 3 – Masking and Plugging
Threaded holes, bearing surfaces and mounting points are protected before coating. Masking and plugging keep bolts turning and parts fitting, which matters when there is only one part and no spare.
Step 4 – Electrostatic Powder Application

Charged powder is applied by electrostatic spray onto the grounded part, so it wraps around tubes, corners and recesses. This helps even coverage on irregular shapes that a flat panel recipe would miss.
Step 5 – Oven Curing

The part moves into the curing oven, where specialty powder coating reaches temperature and hardens. Cure time depends on the powder and the mass of the part, so a heavy casting is planned differently from a thin decorative piece.
Step 6 – Final Inspection and Handoff

We inspect the cured finish for coverage, adhesion and appearance. Typical orders are ready within 48 hours, and unusual jobs are scheduled when we quote. We receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. We also record the colour code and powder used, so a later piece can match.
Our small-batch powder coating schedule keeps parts from waiting between steps, and for a tight lead time, tell us your date at quote.

Quality Standards for Specialty Powder Coating

Our specialty powder coating follows recognized standards: ASTM D3359 for adhesion, ASTM D7091 for dry film thickness and ASTM B117 for salt spray resistance on every order. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, and test reports are available on request.

Quality starts at intake and ends at handoff. After curing, a good finish looks even in colour and gloss, with no thin spots, runs or bare edges. Edges, welds and recesses get particular attention because thin spots usually appear there. We flag any concern with you before parts leave the shop.

An adhesion test checks that the coating bonds to the metal. Dry film thickness readings confirm the coating is neither too thin to protect nor too thick to fit. The salt spray test measures corrosion resistance in a controlled chamber. It is a comparison tool rather than a promise of real-world life, so we explain what results mean for your specialty powder coating order.

Because a unique piece has no second chance, each part is checked before it leaves the shop. Careful finishing of a one-off piece also depends on clean prep and correct curing, so every order follows the same documented steps. Good rust protection comes from that prep and cure, not from colour alone. See our [certification](/certification) page for details.

Businesses and Makers That Use Specialty Powder Coating

Machine shops, fabricators, artists, builders and facility managers use our specialty powder coating most. These customers want a dependable finish on parts that are unusual, hard to replace or built to order, whether they send one piece or a small matched set.

See how we support [powder coating for machine shops](/industries/machine-shops), who often send precision pieces with threads and bores that need masking, and [powder coating for municipalities](/industries/municipal-institutional), who need tough finishes on custom public metalwork.
Specialty Powder Coating FAQs

Short answer: we run specialty powder coating on unusual, one-off and custom metal parts, with fast turnaround on typical orders. These answers cover project fit, timing, matching and logistics so you know what to expect before you book. Ask us anything else before you send parts.

blocks.q: Can you coat a single piece?
blocks.a: Yes. Our small-batch powder coating covers single pieces and small sets, from a repaired bracket to a finished sculpture. Send photos and dimensions with your request, and a project consultation at quote confirms how your part will be coated.

blocks.q: Can you coat a prototype before the design is final?
blocks.a: Yes. Prototypes often change, so tell us the metal, size and finish you expect. Coating a test part shows how the finish behaves before you commit to more.

blocks.q: When will my custom piece be ready?
blocks.a: Typical specialty powder coating orders follow our 48-hour turnaround. Large, heavy or complex jobs are scheduled at quote based on size and prep. We receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.

blocks.q: Can you match the finish of an existing piece?
blocks.a: Yes. Send the piece or a RAL code, and we confirm the powder and colour at quote. Because colour depends on the powder and the metal, we explain any difference before coating.

blocks.q: What if my part has deep recesses or tight areas?
blocks.a: Electrostatic powder wraps around many shapes, but deep recesses can limit coverage. Tell us about hard-to-reach areas, and we plan masking and coating before we start.

blocks.q: How should I prepare a fragile or unique part for drop-off?
blocks.a: Contact us first so we can plan handling. Pack the part so coating surfaces stay clear, and tell us which areas are fit-critical. Pickup and delivery details are confirmed at quote, and drop-off at 10874 Steeles Ave E, Milton, is open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.
